name: education
appliesTo: Schools, tutoring centres, extra classes, LMS, edtech. Teachers, students and parents all read the same product and must not be addressed the same way.

address.teacher: thầy cô — covers either gender. Where a neutral noun reads better: giáo viên.
address.parent: anh/chị. Their child is con, never em — em is what the teacher calls them.
address.self: bên mình, the product name, or no subject

extraRules.caseNote: Case-insensitive on purpose: `cô` opens a sentence as often as it sits inside one, and a case-sensitive pattern misses every `Cô …` — which is exactly where the wrong form of address is most visible.
extraRules.why: A bare `cô` addresses a woman, which excludes half the teachers using the product. It regresses easily when the first user happens to be female.
extraRules.instead: thầy cô, or giáo viên where a neutral noun reads better

extraRules.why: On a parent-facing report this reads as a verdict on their child, and the report is the only surface a stranger judges the product by.
extraRules.instead: nên luyện thêm, chưa vững phần này — describe the gap, not the child

glossary.why: One word per operation. Two words for the same thing reads as two people wrote the app.

notes: Softeners on failures and requests only. Field errors, buttons and status chips stay bare. The student runtime is the shortest copy in the product — a teenager on a phone, mid-test, and submitting a test is not an achievement.
